title: Cap. 6 Arg. 6 open: If grace turns on human disparity, Gospel and faith get an easy human account
pass_a_gloss: If, Christ's death having been supposed, the gift or denial of grace to particular persons proceeds by God's decree not from the absolute liberty of the divine will, but from the disparity of human wills and actions, then it is easy and ready for anyone to give a reason why the Gospel was denied to this nation, why it was granted to another; and why to these particular human beings faith, vivifying and regenerating grace, is given, to others not given. For on the side of those who have it the answer is made, that they were endowed with the light of the Gospel because they used the light of nature well, or less badly; on the side of those who do not have it the answer is made, that they remain destitute of the light of the Gospel because they used the light of nature less well. So among Christians, if it is asked why this one has faith and regenerating grace, that one does not; on the side of those who have it the answer is likewise made, Because they willed to believe, and were unwilling to place an obstacle; on the side of those who do not have it, Because they were unwilling to believe, because they were unwilling to remove the obstacle of grace. Meanwhile concerning the special calling according to purpose, by which God powerfully bends to believing the hearts of those whom he specially wills to pity, there is not a word.
pass_b_english: Suppose Christ's death is granted, and yet by God's decree the gift or denial of grace to particular persons does not proceed from the absolute liberty of the divine will, but from the disparity of human wills and actions. Then anyone can give a ready reason why the Gospel was withheld from this nation and granted to that one, and why these particular people receive faith and vivifying, regenerating grace while others do not. Of those who have it, the story runs: they got the light of the Gospel because they used nature's light well, or at least less badly. Of those who lack it: they stay without Gospel light because they used nature's light less well. Ask among Christians why this person has faith and regenerating grace and that one does not, and you hear the same human ledger—those who have it willed to believe and would not raise an obstacle; those who lack it would not believe and would not clear the obstacle away. Of the special calling according to purpose, by which God powerfully turns the hearts of those he specially chooses to pity toward belief, there is meantime not a word.
source_text: Si supposita morte Christi, ex decreto Dei donatio aut denegatio gratiae singularibus personis, non ex absoluta libertate voluntatis Divinae, sed ex disparitate voluntatum & actionum humanarum procedat, tum facile & promptum est cuivis rationem reddere cur huic nationi denegatum fuerit Evangelium, cur alteri concessum; & cur hisce singularibus hominibus detur fides, gratia vivificans & regenerans, aliis non detur. Ex parte etenim habentium respondetur, Eos Evangelii luce donatos, quia luce naturae bene, aut minus male, usi fuerint; Ex parte non-habentium respondetur, Eos Evangelii luce destitutos manere, quia lumine naturae minus bene usi fuerint. Sic inter Christianos, si quaeratur cur hic fidem habet & gratiam regenerantem, ille non habet; ex parte habentium etiam respondetur, Quia voluerunt credere, & noluerunt obicem ponere; ex parte non-habentium, Quia noluerunt credere, quia noluerunt obicem gratiae removere. Interim de speciali & secundum propositum vocatione, qua Deus eorum quos specialiter misereri vult corda potenter flectit ad credendum, verbum nullum.
